title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 61
paragraphs: So, starting from Eretria after a lapse of ten years, they returned. In Attica the first place of which they took possession was Marathon. While they were encamped there, their partisans from the city came out to them, and others also flowed in from the various demes—men to whom tyrannical rule was more welcome than freedom. So these were gathering themselves together, but the Athenians in the city, so long as Peisistratus was collecting the money, and afterwards when he took possession of Marathon, made no account of it. But when they heard that he was marching from Marathon toward the city, then they went out to the rescue against him. So these were going in full force to fight against the returning exiles, and the forces of Peisistratus, as they went toward the city starting from Marathon, met them just as they came to the temple of Athena Pallenis, where they encamped opposite. Then, moved by divine guidance, there came into the presence of Peisistratus one Amphilytus of Acarnania, a soothsayer, who approaching him uttered an oracle in hexameter verse, speaking thus:
“The cast has been made, and the net has been widely spread; in the night the tunnies will dart through the moon-lit waters.”
